rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named; mood-floor 8+/10 on teaching beats.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fresh trace (regenerated, see cache): opener=8, Phase 1 (skill invocation)=8, Phase 2 (read map)=8, Phase 3 (delta)=9, close=8 — all teaching beats clear the 8-floor, no beat below 7. Two beats correctly classified setup/optional and mood-exempt (null): 'Kick off the run, then work the other window' (folded into Phase 1's phase entry — compresses to a parenthetical without breaking the arc) and 'Phase 4: Add the context header' (explicitly optional, 'Your call').

Sharpening language throughout is inquiry-framed, not shame-framed: 'is that reason true for this codebase, or true for any codebase?' and 'Look again at the part of your feature you'd describe as the weird bit' (maintainer push-backs) read as curiosity, not correction of a mistake. Body's own 'Push back until the reason names your codebase' names a discipline to practice, not a failure to confess.

Read what it surfaces. Decide: which surface did it flag that you'd underweighted? What did it miss that you know matters? Name the delta — this is the access-mapping that STRIDE will consume.' File delivers exactly this shape (curated-breadth vs. codebase-specific-judgment split matches strategy's 'we curate; you build' claim verbatim in spirit). No front-run: STRIDE's threat-categorization and Ex3's test-strategy authoring are correctly deferred, only named as 'what this sets up' / a parallel window, never taught here. The new opener chunk ('Take the ranked ten, leave the rest on disk') matches the strategy doc's reading-contract rule #3 exactly ('M3 takes it into use where outputs first get big') without front-running the module's separate closer beat (control-is-interrogation / branch-is-the-permission), which the strategy doc places elsewhere in M3's arc, not in this Ex1 file. Close hands off with stakes intact ('if you rushed Phase 2, STRIDE threat-models a thin map') rather than declaring the earned-trust arc resolved — mood does not resolve early.
